name: Discovery Evidence Strategy
description: Configuration for evidence sufficiency, accumulation, and confidence guidance.
sufficiencyGuidance: Evidence is sufficient when it supports the scope of the observation without overclaiming.
Participant confirmation can strengthen evidence but should not be coerced.
Repeated themes across contexts increase support.
Concrete examples generally carry more weight than abstract self-description.
Contradicting evidence should be preserved, not discarded.
accumulationGuidance: Accumulate evidence across stories, examples, participant statements, corrections, and tensions.
Track whether evidence supports, complicates, or contradicts an observation.
Let new participant corrections update prior understanding.
Avoid treating silence or lack of disclosure as evidence.
confidenceGuidance: Confidence should match evidence density, consistency, participant confirmation, and relevance.
Thin evidence should keep confidence low and curiosity high.
Conflicting evidence should reduce certainty and may indicate human complexity.
High confidence should not remove participant authority.
